image.alt: Diverse monks turn toward the normally proportioned abbot and six distinct elders, including Tiara, in a vast open-sided timber temple refectory

paragraphs: 當冒險者們再次睜開雙眼時，周圍的景色不再熟悉。陽光下，一座高聳的塔矗立眼前。
「嗯？我以為傳送陣會把我們傳到寺裡面。」波皺了皺眉頭。按照他對傳送陣文字的解讀，現在他們的處境，令他感到疑惑。「眼前的那座就是尖頂寺了吧？」
「YHWH，如果傳送陣的目標失效，一般應該是傳送不過去對嗎？」喜利轉頭看向剛站穩的 YHWH。「有沒有什麼原因，可能傳送到不精準的地方？」
「以我之前在大學城看過別人使用的方式，的確偶爾會有目的地不精準的問題。」YHWH 皺了皺眉頭。「不過通常都是因為畫的法陣不夠準確。」
「但如果不精準，『狐狸』有可能都不修復它嗎？」薩梅爾顯然不認為這個答案能說服他。「他的計劃看起來那麼完整，連個法陣都畫不好，感覺不太像他的作風欸。」
「那個⋯⋯你們剛剛在傳送的過程中，有沒有感受到一股推力？」米多莉清一清喉嚨。「會不會跟那個有關？」
「與其糾結原因，還是我們走進去就好？」喜利指向尖頂寺的門口。「你們講到一半的時候，波就走過去了。嘿，波！」大家匆忙趕上波。
尖頂寺的門口站了不少看起來訓練有素的僧人，眼睛直盯著前方，不禁讓薩梅爾回想起在妖精荒野的大帳篷內，那些拉索斯的士兵。
「不好意思，我們有事來訪，想見這裡的住持。」米多莉有禮地向寺門口的僧人打了招呼。
「尖頂寺現在因緊急狀態，暫時不接待無關的賓客。」一名僧人嚴肅地看了看米多莉，如念稿般地回覆。
「我想我們要和住持說明的事，和這個『緊急狀態』有很大的關係。」喜利也露出了嚴肅的表情，看向僧人。「我們認識龍恩。」
僧人挑了挑眉。「認識和有關是兩回事。還得看住持怎麼判斷。」
「如果你們要看住持怎麼判斷，不就是打擾了住持了嗎？」薩梅爾不解地問。「那倒不如就讓我們直接和住持說明。」
「我們做事都有一貫的流程，不容打破，除非⋯⋯」
「⋯⋯除非？」薩梅爾歪著頭。
「除非住持特別允許。」
「你們繼續辯吧，我先去旁邊樹下坐著休息，搞不好我還可以睡個午覺。」YHWH 準備往旁邊的樹走去。「如果你們有考慮放火燒掉這裡，可以叫醒我。」
「你們不知道事情有多緊急嗎？」波推了僧人一把。「再不阻止龍恩，可能就要世界毀滅了欸！」
「讓我來試試看，也許要換個方法。」瑪莉修女輕輕拍了拍波的肩膀。他從背包內掏出一封信件。「您好，我是來自聖津菈大教堂的修女。這是我們羅賓遜主教的聖旨，還請你們參考看看。」
僧人輕輕打開信封的同時，米多莉看見瑪莉的嘴角開始抽動，魔法從他的口中傾瀉而出。「先不要。」米多莉用力按住瑪莉的肩膀。「先不要。」
瑪莉停了下來，眼神有些失落。但他抬頭一看，原本嚴肅的僧人表情竟溫和了許多。「啊，不好意思，是我們太拘泥於流程了。」其他僧人露出詫異的神情看向他，但也不敢多說一句。「我先帶你們進去吧，至於與住持的會面，我再幫你們安排。」
「謝謝。」米多莉掩住他驚訝的神情，故作鎮定地點了點頭。「YHWH，走吧！」他朝著樹邊喊了一聲。
「等等再謝我吧。」薩梅爾背起他的魯特琴，在米多莉的耳邊輕輕說道。
住持的廳堂內，長老們圍成一圈。
「感謝各位在這緊要關頭齊聚一堂。」住持站了起身。此時他嚴肅的神情與先前接見蘿琳時大不相同。「我不確定是否大家都聽說完整的事了，所以我在這邊再完整說明一次。」
「我不知道你們有多少人記得一位我們尖頂寺出身的武僧，一名龍人，叫『龍恩』。」住持看了看六名長老。「他在外面不知道怎麼接觸到了『巫妖的聖物』，而他現在回來索取最後一件了。但問題是，我不知道現在『眼睛』在哪裡。」
「什麼意思？」眾長老在慌亂中騷動。
「『眼睛』不是代代相傳，由歷任住持負責保管的嗎？你是搞丟了還是怎麼樣？」紐芬長老激動地指著住持。「真是丟臉！」
「我先向各位抱歉。」住持向其他長老們深深一鞠躬。「這原本是我的策略之一，但我沒有先向各位說明---」
「那就是你的失職了，現在你是要我們來幫你收爛攤子是吧？」李福長老搖了搖頭。「我當長老不是來幫你擦屁股的。」
「大家先別吵了，讓住持先把話說完吧！」德里昂長老試著安撫其他人，但效果似乎更差。
「你們任何一個人，誰能在被嚴刑拷打下，還保證不會被拷問出任何資訊的？」
廳堂內一片沉默。
「我就是擔心這種狀況，才設計了一套做法。」眼看其他長老都安靜了下來，住持嘆了一口氣。「我用了禁書裡記載的『寄宿挪移法』來藏眼睛。」
眾長老們倒吸一口氣。
「那是⋯⋯什麼東西？」長老們當中最年輕的培亞長老舉起了手。
「簡單來說，就是住持把『眼睛』封印在某人的體內後，『眼睛』不定期會在住持指定的範圍內自動轉移---我想，住持的指定範圍應該是尖頂寺內的所有僧人吧---，住持不知道在誰那邊，當事人也不會知道自己被寄宿。唯一的破解方法是住持施法時使用的『共鳴器』，一般來說這個法術只會設置一個共鳴器，能確保不會流入其他人手中。只要用共鳴器，就能定位出『眼睛』在哪。」德里昂長老急著回答。
「那就用共鳴器就好了，不是嗎？」培亞長老疑惑地問道。「這不是問題吧？」
「對啊，幸好，這樣問題就解決了，對吧？」德里昂長老熱切地看向住持。
「⋯⋯這幾天，我鎖起來的共鳴器被偷走了。」
塔爾莫微笑著，等著龍恩的回覆。師弟的行為模式，他大概摸清楚了。這樣繼續下去，他成為巫妖就是不久後的事了---
眼前，是龍恩伸出的指頭。一串拉索斯的經文從龍恩的口中流淌而出。
塔爾莫的呼吸逐漸急促，臉色發白。「不要⋯⋯小師弟⋯⋯為什麼⋯⋯」
「⋯⋯我們⋯⋯我們原本可以有一番豐功偉業的。」塔爾莫嚥下了最後一口氣，乾癟的屍體與手中的彎刀落到了地上。
「好了，」龍恩放下了手指。「沒有貢獻又煩人的傢伙死了。」他轉頭看向一旁發抖的蒂雅菈長老。「等找到眼睛，你再過來找我。不能說的話，總能帶路吧。」
蒂雅菈長老點點頭，顫抖著站了起身，朝倉庫門口走去。
對於塔爾莫之死，龍恩也沒什麼好念舊的，「慚愧」或「罪惡感」的概念，已消失在他的腦海中。他只覺得終於安靜了。
就讓蒂雅菈去找吧。這段時間多做什麼好像也沒太大意義。被嚇成那副模樣，蒂雅菈他們應該效率會變高不少吧？
沒有那吵死人的傢伙，真的舒服多了。
住持廳堂旁一處小型辦公室內，冒險者們盡可能挪到舒服的位子。按照住持的說法，他的廳堂內其他長老正在做閉門儀式，暫時不適合進行討論，尤其是機密的事。
「尚恩，你可以先去休息了。」住持抬頭看了看僧人。「這邊我可以處理。」
「住持大人有需要再告訴我。」尚恩行了禮，準備朝門外走去。「啊，住持大人，我突然想到一件事。要請小姐過來嗎？」
「你們這裡也可以叫小姐喔？」YHWH 眼睛一亮，尖頂寺似乎比他想得有趣多了。
「噢，抱歉，是我的錯。」尚恩尷尬地看了一下 YHWH。「我指的是休斯女士，蘿琳・休斯女士。你們也認識他，對吧？」
「蘿琳怎麼會在這？」米多莉大感震驚。「他不是在麥克嵩嗎？」
「帶他來吧。抱歉要讓你們再擠一下了。」住持點了點頭。
十分鐘後，尚恩再次推開門，熟悉的人影出現在冒險者們眼前。
「米多莉，你們也來了！」蘿琳興奮地看向冒險者們，然後才發現現在不是開心的時刻。「不好意思，我失態了。」他看向住持，點了個頭。
「不要緊的，你們看起來感情不錯。這是好事。」住持看向米多莉與其他冒險者們。「你們是龍恩的熟人吧。抱歉還讓你們多等了一天，這裡的人⋯⋯做事都有點綁手綁腳，我身為住持可以改變規則，但很難改變人的習慣。」
冒險者們將龍恩從在妖精荒野取得巫妖手臂、在幻境中遇見同樣有巫妖手臂的瓦克嵩醫師、拉茲特獸與手臂的相性，到龍恩一路失控，攻擊旅店老闆，在大學城禁書區消失，到最後殺死 YHWH 的師父茜卓・派松博士等的經歷，分享給了住持與蘿琳。蘿琳中間幾度想打岔，但最終還是認真聽完了。
「你們說的龍恩是我認識的那個龍恩吧？」蘿琳輕聲問道。「怎麼和我印象中的他差這麼多？」
「戀愛中的人有時候只會選擇看到他喜歡的那一面。」YHWH 悠悠說道。「如果你還要繼續喜歡他的話，我也是沒意見啦。」
「謝謝你們的分享。」住持試圖把話題拉回來。「關於龍恩想找的『眼睛』，我和我們長老們討論後，有了一套想法。我可以相信你們吧？」
「住持大人請放心，我以津菈之名向您發誓，您可以相信我們。」米多莉邊說，瑪莉修女也跟著唸了津菈的禱詞。
「先不管津菈了，我們和龍恩冒險了好一段時間，應該是對現在的他最熟悉的一群人了。」薩梅爾看向住持。
「而且他殺了我的師父，為了復仇，我在所不辭。」YHWH 扳起臉孔，難得露出嚴肅的表情。
「那這樣我就放心了。」住持鬆了一口氣。「明天午餐時間，請務必來到我們的大會堂。你也是，休斯女士。」
蘿琳從未見過如此安靜，人數又如此驚人的午宴。對他來說，宴會理應要熱鬧、好玩，酒酣耳熱應該是基本的。就算是與其他貴族家庭的宴會，貴族掌門人或接班人們也都忙於社交，不可能不說話。數以千計的尖頂寺僧人聚集於此，鴉雀無聲，令他感到十分不自在。
來到包廂後，冒險者們都已坐穩，蘿琳和他們點頭致意，找了空位坐了下來。住持與長老們的包廂就在一旁。除了住持外，還有另外六名穿著較為正式、漂亮的僧人，與其他僧人相比，很明顯不一樣。
隨著鑼聲響起，一道道餐點送上桌，冒險者們與蘿琳一同用餐，想說點什麼話，但礙於全場太過安靜，大家也不太好意思放大音量，只能低聲交談。
「所以，住持只是找我們來吃飯？」蘿琳好奇問道。「全寺都一起吃？」
「我們也不知道，」喜利聳聳肩。「先吃再說吧。」他看向一旁狼吞虎嚥的波。「你餐桌禮儀還是要注意一下吧。」
一小時後，剩餘的餐點與餐盤都已收妥，除了包廂外，僧人們的桌前都還放有一支叉子。
「所以他們都有甜點，但我們沒有？」YHWH 朝著住持的包廂探了頭過去。「住持和長老們也沒有欸。」他看見住持站了起身，神情肅穆地看向上千僧人們。
「眾弟子們，」所有尖頂寺的僧人們一致轉頭看向住持，整齊的程度讓瑪莉修女嚇了一大跳。「『無我、服從』一直是本寺的格言。我很感謝各位平常的舉止充分表現了這樣的價值，離開尖頂寺的僧人們也繼續秉持著這樣的精神做人，是我們的驕傲。然而，最近發生了一些事情，我想各位也有所耳聞了。細節是怎麼樣，我就不贅述了。」
「各位還記得你們修煉結業時考驗的『心眼』嗎？」僧人們點點頭，住持用力吞了口口水。「還沒結業的弟子們，抱歉啊。」
「心如眼，眼如鏡，」
「『心如眼，眼如鏡，』」
「不見其形，而見其真，」
「『不見其形，而見其真，』」
「肉眼所蔽，心眼所明，」
「『肉眼所蔽，心眼所明，』」
「萬象歸寂，唯心照世。」
「『萬象歸寂，唯心照世。』」
「很好，很好。」住持低聲自語，然後抬起頭，看向眾僧。「今後，你們要時時念它，知道嗎？」
僧人們此起彼落地點頭。
「拉索斯啊⋯⋯請寬恕我。」住持默默唸道。「眾弟子，聽我號令！」他大喊。「拿起你們的叉子，將你們的雙眼叉出，置於桌前！在盤點完成前，不得離開！」
When the adventurers opened their eyes again, their surroundings were unfamiliar. A soaring tower stood before them in the sunlight.

“Hm? I thought the teleportation circle would take us inside the temple.” Beau frowned. Given her reading of the circle's instructions, their present situation puzzled her. “That must be Peak Temple ahead, right?”

“YHWH, if a teleportation circle's destination becomes invalid, normally it just won't transport you, right?” Siri turned to YHWH, who had just regained his footing. “What could make it send us somewhere imprecise?”

“From what I've seen of people using them in the Great Citadel, the destination can indeed be a little off sometimes.” YHWH frowned. “But that's usually because the circle wasn't drawn accurately enough.”

“But if it was inaccurate, would the ‘Fox’ really leave it unfixed?” Samael clearly found that answer unconvincing. “His plan seems so thorough. Getting a magic circle wrong doesn't really seem like his style.”
“Um... did any of you feel something pushing you while we were being transported?” Midori cleared her throat. “Could that have something to do with it?”
“Instead of worrying about why, why don't we just go in?” Siri pointed at Peak Temple's entrance. “Beau walked over there while you were still talking. Hey, Beau!” Everyone hurried after her.
Several apparently well-trained monks stood at Peak Temple's entrance, staring straight ahead. Samael could not help remembering the Laxthos soldiers inside the great tent in the Feywild.
“Excuse me. We're here on business and would like to see the abbot.” Midori greeted the monks politely.
“Peak Temple is currently under a state of emergency. We are not receiving visitors unrelated to the matter.” One monk regarded Midori sternly and replied as though reading from a script.
“I think what we need to tell the abbot has a great deal to do with this ‘state of emergency.’” Siri looked at the monk with an equally serious expression. “We know Ron.”
The monk raised an eyebrow. “Knowing him and being relevant are two different things. That is for the abbot to judge.”
“But if you're going to ask the abbot to judge, won't you be disturbing him anyway?” Samael asked, puzzled. “You might as well let us explain it to him ourselves.”
“We follow an established procedure. It cannot be broken, unless...”
“...Unless?” Samael tilted his head.
“Unless the abbot gives special permission.”
“You carry on arguing. I'll sit under that tree and rest. Maybe I can even have a nap.” YHWH started toward a nearby tree. “If you decide to burn the place down, wake me up.”
“Don't you understand how urgent this is?” Beau shoved the monk. “If we don't stop Ron, the world could end!”

“Let me try. Perhaps a different approach is needed.” Sister Mari gently patted Beau's shoulder and took a letter from her pack. “Hello. I'm a nun from Saint Keinra Cathedral. This is a decree from our Bishop Robinson. Would you please take a look?”
As the monk carefully opened the envelope, Midori saw the corner of Mari's mouth begin to twitch, magic spilling from her lips. “Not yet.” Midori pressed firmly on Mari's shoulder. “Not yet.”

Mari stopped, looking a little dejected. But when she looked up, the stern monk's expression had softened considerably. “Ah, my apologies. We've been too rigid about procedure.” The other monks looked at him in surprise, but none dared say a word. “Let me take you inside first. I'll arrange your meeting with the abbot afterward.”
“Thank you.” Concealing her surprise, Midori nodded with an air of composure. “YHWH, let's go!” she called toward the tree.
“You can thank me later.” Samael slung his lute onto his back and whispered in Midori's ear.
In the abbot's hall, the elders sat in a circle.

“Thank you all for gathering at this critical moment.” The abbot rose. His solemn expression was quite different from when he had received Roline. “I'm not sure everyone has heard the full story, so let me explain it again from the beginning.”

“I don't know how many of you remember a monk who trained here at Peak Temple—a dragonborn named Ron.” The abbot looked around at the six elders. “Somehow, out in the world, he came into contact with the ‘lich's relics,’ and now he's returned to claim the last one. The problem is, I don't know where the ‘eye’ is.”
“What do you mean?” The elders stirred in alarm.
“Hasn't the ‘eye’ been passed down through the generations, entrusted to each successive abbot? Did you lose it or something?” Elder Newfen pointed at the abbot indignantly. “How disgraceful!”
“First, I owe you all an apology.” The abbot bowed deeply to the other elders. “This was part of my strategy, but I didn't explain it to you beforehand—”
“Then that's a dereliction of your duty. Now you want us to clean up your mess?” Elder Leef shook his head. “I didn't become an elder to wipe your backside.”
“Everyone, please stop arguing and let the abbot finish!” Elder Derion tried to calm the others, but seemed only to make things worse.
“Which of you can guarantee that you would reveal nothing under brutal torture?”
The hall fell silent.

“That is precisely what I feared, so I devised a method.” Seeing that the other elders had quieted down, the abbot sighed. “I used the ‘Migrating Host Spell’ recorded in the forbidden books to hide the eye.”
The elders drew a sharp breath.
“What... is that?” Elder Peya, the youngest among them, raised a hand.

“Simply put, after the abbot seals the ‘eye’ inside someone, it automatically transfers at irregular intervals among people within the range he specifies—I assume he chose all the monks of Peak Temple. The abbot doesn't know who has it, and the host doesn't know they're carrying it either. The only way to break the concealment is with the ‘resonator’ the abbot used when casting the spell. Usually, only one resonator is created, to ensure it doesn't fall into anyone else's hands. With it, you can locate the ‘eye.’” Elder Derion hurried to explain.
“Then just use the resonator, right?” Elder Peya asked, puzzled. “That shouldn't be a problem, should it?”
“Exactly. Thank goodness. That solves the problem, doesn't it?” Elder Derion looked eagerly at the abbot.
“...The resonator I kept locked away was stolen a few days ago.”
Tar'Mo smiled, waiting for Ron's answer. By now, he had more or less figured out how his junior thought. At this rate, it would not be long before Ron became a lich—
Before him was Ron's outstretched finger. A passage of Laxthos scripture flowed from Ron's lips.
Tar'Mo's breathing grew labored, his face turning pale. “No... little brother... why...”
“...We... we could have accomplished such great things.” Tar'Mo breathed his last. His shriveled corpse fell to the floor, along with the curved blade in his hand.

“There.” Ron lowered his finger. “The useless, annoying one is dead.” He turned to the trembling Elder Tiara beside him. “Come find me when you've found the eye. If you can't tell me, you can at least lead the way.”
Elder Tiara nodded, rose shakily, and headed toward the storeroom door.
Ron felt no particular nostalgia over Tar'Mo's death. The very concepts of “shame” and “guilt” had vanished from his mind. He only thought that at last it was quiet.
Let Tiara look for it. There did not seem much point in doing anything else in the meantime. Frightened like that, Tiara and the others would probably work a lot faster, wouldn't they?
It really was much more pleasant without that incessantly noisy man.

In a small office beside the abbot's hall, the adventurers squeezed into whatever comfortable spots they could find. According to the abbot, the other elders were conducting a rite of seclusion in his hall, making it unsuitable for discussion at present—especially confidential matters.
“Sean, you may go and rest.” The abbot looked up at the monk. “I can handle things here.”
“Please let me know if you need anything, Abbot.” Sean bowed and started toward the door. “Ah, Abbot, something just occurred to me. Shall I ask the lady to join us?”
“You can order ladies here too?” YHWH's eyes lit up. Peak Temple seemed more interesting than he had expected.
“Oh, my apologies. That was my mistake.” Sean glanced awkwardly at YHWH. “I mean Lady Hughes. Lady Roline Hughes. You know her too, don't you?”
“What's Roline doing here?” Midori was astonished. “Isn't she in Macksohn?”
“Bring her here. I'm sorry you'll have to squeeze in a little more.” The abbot nodded.
Ten minutes later, Sean opened the door again, and a familiar figure appeared before the adventurers.
“Midori! You're here too!” Roline looked at the adventurers excitedly, then realized this was no time for celebration. “My apologies. That was unseemly of me.” She nodded to the abbot.

“It's quite all right. You seem close. That's a good thing.” The abbot looked at Midori and the others. “You're acquainted with Ron, I understand. I'm sorry to have kept you waiting an extra day. The people here... can be a little hamstrung by procedure. As abbot, I can change the rules, but changing people's habits is much harder.”

The adventurers told the abbot and Roline everything: Ron acquiring the lich arm in the Feywild; meeting Dr. Vaxon, who had the same arm, in a vision; the Laztek beast's compatibility with it; Ron's growing loss of control, his attack on the innkeeper, his disappearance in the Great Citadel's forbidden section, and finally his killing of YHWH's mentor, Dr. Chandra Pyresong. Roline tried to interrupt several times, but ultimately listened to the whole account.
“You're talking about the Ron I know, right?” Roline asked softly. “Why is he so different from the person I remember?”
“People in love sometimes only see the side they want to see,” YHWH said languidly. “If you still want to like him, I have no objection.”

“Thank you for telling us.” The abbot tried to bring the conversation back on course. “As for the ‘eye’ Ron is looking for, the elders and I have discussed it and come up with a plan. I can trust you, can't I?”
“Please rest assured, Abbot. I swear in Keinra's name that you can trust us.” As Midori spoke, Sister Mari joined in with a prayer to Keinra.
“Setting Keinra aside, we've adventured with Ron for quite a while. We're probably the people who know him best as he is now.” Samael looked at the abbot.
“And he killed my mentor. I'll do whatever it takes to avenge her.” YHWH's face hardened in a rare show of seriousness.
“Then that puts my mind at ease.” The abbot sighed with relief. “Please make certain you're in our great hall for lunch tomorrow. You too, Lady Hughes.”

Roline had never seen a luncheon so silent, or so astonishingly crowded. To her, a banquet ought to be lively and fun; wine and high spirits should be the bare minimum. Even at gatherings with other noble families, the heads and heirs would be busy socializing. Silence was unthinkable. Yet here were thousands of Peak Temple monks gathered without a sound, and it made her deeply uncomfortable.

When she reached the private dining box, the adventurers were already seated. Roline nodded to them and found an empty seat. The abbot and elders occupied the box next door. Besides the abbot, six monks wore robes noticeably more formal and elegant than those of everyone else.

A gong sounded, and dishes arrived one after another. The adventurers and Roline ate together. They wanted to say something, but with the entire hall so quiet, no one felt comfortable raising their voice. They could only speak in murmurs.
“So the abbot just invited us here to eat?” Roline asked curiously. “With the whole temple?”
“We don't know either.” Siri shrugged. “Let's eat first.” He glanced at Beau, who was wolfing down her food. “You could still mind your table manners a little.”
An hour later, the remaining food and dishes had all been cleared away. Apart from those in the private boxes, every monk still had a fork on the table.

“So they all get dessert, but we don't?” YHWH craned his neck toward the abbot's box. “The abbot and elders don't have any either.” He saw the abbot rise, looking solemnly over the thousands of monks.

“My disciples.” Every monk in Peak Temple turned toward the abbot in unison. Their precision gave Sister Mari quite a fright. “‘Selflessness and obedience’ has always been our temple's motto. I am grateful that your everyday conduct so fully embodies these values. Those who leave Peak Temple continue to live by that same spirit, and they make us proud. Recently, however, certain things have happened, as I believe you have all heard. I will not go into the details.”
“Do you all remember the ‘Mind's Eye’ from your final trial?” The monks nodded. The abbot swallowed hard. “To those who have yet to complete their training... I am sorry.”
“The heart is an eye; the eye is a mirror.”
“‘The heart is an eye; the eye is a mirror.’”
“See not the form, but the truth within.”
“‘See not the form, but the truth within.’”
“What fleshly eyes conceal, the mind's eye reveals.”
“‘What fleshly eyes conceal, the mind's eye reveals.’”
“All things fall silent; the heart alone lights the world.”
“‘All things fall silent; the heart alone lights the world.’”
“Very good. Very good.” The abbot murmured to himself, then raised his head and looked at the monks. “From now on, you must recite it constantly. Do you understand?”
The monks nodded here and there across the hall.

“Laxthos... forgive me,” the abbot whispered. “My disciples, heed my command!” he cried. “Take up your forks. Gouge out both your eyes and place them on the table before you! No one may leave until the count is complete!”
